steps: Removing a middle cue retains the next cue’s track identity; adding a selected-track play and stop, reviewing, changing languages and cancelling never writes author data. Existing audio JSON opens the independent native-backed editor. Changes to volume, independent looping, cue time and restart action survive Chinese/English/Japanese at 390px with visible return/cancel/review/apply controls; review and Cancel leave both the draft and author tree unchanged.
Removing every cue is reviewed, applied only to the ordinary draft and saved. Reopening accepts the empty timeline, retaining both tracks, all metadata and the original WAV.
Apply changes only the ordinary unsaved source draft. Ordinary Save updates exactly the reviewed audio JSON; metadata, scene, referenced WAV and other author files remain byte-identical.

The same scene plans, builds and runs through real Godot. The host validates four audio commands (music play, effect play at 0.125s, music and effect stop at 0.5s in author order) and independent audio/actor completion.

Chrome downloads the generated engine project ZIP. Independent verification confirms one deduplicated WAV resource, extraction preserves its exact bytes and settings, and fresh Godot import/run at another path produces identical audio events.
